name: Large power transformers
thesis: The heavy iron that steps power up and down for the grid. Lead times have blown out to ~5 years — under 10% of data-center cost, but effectively 100% of the bottleneck.

gauge.rationale: High-voltage transformer lead times stretched to ~5 years as grid step-up demand ran far ahead of a thin global supplier base.

why_it_gates: No transformer, no interconnect, no power delivered — even with turbines and accelerators ready to go. Large units are made by only a few global firms, the US imports most of its high-voltage transformers, and grain-oriented electrical steel plus skilled labor cap how fast supply can scale. The cheapest line item on the bill of materials has become the schedule-defining one.

catalysts.text: Capacity expansions (GE Vernova/Prolec, Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy)
On-site generation partly bypasses the grid-tie / transformer queue
Grain-oriented electrical steel + labor constraints keep lead times long

what_loosens_it: New transformer plants, added electrical-steel capacity, and on-site generation that reduces grid-tie needs. But PwC expects the supply-demand imbalance to persist for years.

developments.text: High-voltage transformer lead times extend to ~5 years; step-up transformer demand up 274% since 2019
GE Vernova electrification orders roughly doubled YoY; data-center orders hit $2.4B in Q1 alone
